name: Michel Foucault
role: French philosopher and historian of systems of thought (1926-1984)
summary: Foucault analysed how power, knowledge and institutions such as prisons, asylums and sexual norms shape people, and he rejected the idea that knowledge or morality stands outside power. As an activist he campaigned on prisons, abortion, the death penalty, homosexuality and support for Solidarity, and he wrote sympathetically of the 1978-79 Iranian uprising. He avoided setting out a programme, so his stated positions cover only part of the statement bank.

notes: Most of his work is historical analysis of how power operates, not a statement of what policy should be, and such analysis was not counted as a position (premise is not a position). He offered no programme on economy, government structure, world affairs, ecology or technology. Themes searched in the local texts of the Essential Works, Politics Philosophy Culture, Power/Knowledge, the Chomsky debate, Remarks on Marx and the History of Sexuality: economy and welfare (the 1983 social security interview is analysis and answers nothing), government, world, prisons, society, liberty, means, religion, ecology, technology. The 1971 debate comes early; his later writing on revolt and revolution is more guarded, so those answers are low. Texts on age of consent and the Iranian revolution were read but match no statement closely enough to answer. Failing the uncertainty rule is the honest result.
